name: cointegration_pairs_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Cointegrated stock pairs identified via Engle-Granger two-step procedure exhibit stronger mean-reversion properties than simple correlation-based pairs. By running a rolling cointegration test on 5-day intraday data (1500+ bars) and only trading pairs where the ADF test on residuals rejects the unit root at 5%, we filter for pairs with genuine long-run equilibrium relationships. The focus is on SBIN vs PNB (public sector banks with shared government ownership, similar NPA cycles, and correlated lending portfolios). The inefficiency persists because cointegration requires statistical sophistication and rolling computation that most retail traders lack.
stock_filter: Both stocks daily volume > ₹100cr; SBIN lot size compatible with PNB sizing

long.confirmation: coint_residual increases for 2 consecutive bars from trough

short.confirmation: coint_residual decreases for 2 consecutive bars from peak

entry.entry_price: market orders on both legs; PNB position = beta_coint * SBIN_position_shares

exit.stop_loss: z_score exceeds 3.5 OR loss > 0.6% of capital
exit.trailing_stop: once z_score within 0.5 of zero, trail at 0.8 sigma from best
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 90 mins without 50% target progress
exit.signal_exit: if ADF_stat crosses above critical value (cointegration breaks), exit immediately

risk.position_sizing: cointegration-beta-weighted: SBIN shares * price = notional / 2, PNB shares = (notional / 2) / (beta_coint * PNB_price)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22; PSU bank vol spikes in high-VIX environments
filters.volume_filter: SBIN 1-min vol > 50000 shares, PNB > 100000 shares at entry
filters.event_filter: skip if government bank recapitalization or NPA resolution news today
other_filters: skip if cointegration relationship has been rejected for 3+ consecutive days

edge.edge_decay_risk: low-moderate — PSU bank pairs are less traded by quant desks; edge stable for 12+ months

weaknesses: PSU banks are subject to government policy shocks (merger announcements, capital infusion) that can permanently shift the cointegration relationship without warning
PNB has lower liquidity and wider spreads than SBIN, causing asymmetric slippage: the PNB leg often fills worse, creating persistent small drag on returns
Rolling cointegration using 5-day data (1500 bars) is computationally expensive and may lag genuine structural breaks by several hours
prior_art: Engle & Granger (1987) cointegration; Vidyamurthy (2004) cointegration-based pairs trading. Alexander & Dimitriu (2005) for rolling cointegration window calibration.
notes: Edge math: 0.63 * 50bps - 0.37 * 35bps = 31.5 - 12.95 = 18.55bps gross. Costs ~12bps RT. Net ~6.55bps/trade * 3 trades = ~20bps daily. PSU bank pairs have wider spreads (more opportunity) but also more noise. ADF filter is the key edge — only trade statistically confirmed cointegration.
